# Library reference

Every module a Nish program can import, one page each, generated from the doc comments of its source. The builtins come with the compiler; the `nish/` modules are the standard library, written in Nish.

## Builtins

| Module | |
| --- | --- |
| [Globals](builtins.md) | Ambient declarations for the Nish global surface. |
| [`nish:async`](nish-async.md) | Tasks for `async` functions: start one and go on, or await two to eight at once. |
| [`nish:fs`](nish-fs.md) | Files and directories: read, write, rename, remove and list paths on the host's file system. |
| [`nish:io`](nish-io.md) | Text and bytes to stdout and stderr with nothing added, and the panic that ends a program on an unmet invariant. |
| [`nish:net`](nish-net.md) | Non-blocking sockets for a program that owns its loop: TCP, UDP, Unix-domain sockets, and a level-triggered readiness loop to wait on them. |
| [`nish:process`](nish-process.md) | The process and its host: exit, the environment, children, signals, the clocks, scheduling, and the size of the machine. |
| [`nish:region`](nish-region.md) | Memory a program frees when it says so (docs/LANGUAGE.md, "Regions"). |
| [`nish:secret`](nish-secret.md) | Key material, and the rules that keep it in (docs/LANGUAGE.md, "Secrets"). |
| [`nish:simd`](nish-simd.md) | Sixteen-byte vectors of one lane type, and the lane-wise operations on them, each lowered to target-independent LLVM vector IR. |
| [`nish:term`](nish-term.md) | Terminal input for a full-screen program: read a key the moment it is pressed, wait for one with a timeout that doubles as a frame clock, and ask the terminal whether it is one, how big it is, and to stop echoing. |
| [`nish:unsafe`](nish-unsafe.md) | Element access with no bounds check, signed arithmetic that wraps, and a C string read through a pointer nothing proves. |

## Standard library

| Module | |
| --- | --- |
| [`nish/base64`](base64.md) | Standard base64 (RFC 4648 §4) with `=` padding, the encoding kitty graphics frames are sent in. |
| [`nish/bytes`](bytes.md) | Fixed-width integers and doubles read from, and written into, a byte array at an offset, in either byte order. |
| [`nish/cli-args`](cli-args.md) | A command tree for a large command-line tool: declared once with a builder, parsed in one walk over the arguments, and answered as the matched command's id and every value with where it came from. |
| [`nish/cli-flags`](cli-flags.md) | A command line's flags, declared once as data and read back by name, with the same declaration writing the `--help` rows. |
| [`nish/cli`](cli.md) | A command-line tool's help menu: whether a stream gets colour, the escapes that paint it, and the rows a `--help` is made of. |
| [`nish/collections`](collections.md) | The global `Map` and `Set` (docs/wp32-map.md). |
| [`nish/compress/checksum`](compress/checksum.md) | The two checksums the compressed formats carry: CRC-32 (ISO 3309, the polynomial gzip's trailer uses, RFC 1952 §8) and Adler-32 (zlib's trailer, RFC 1950 §9). |
| [`nish/compress/deflate`](compress/deflate.md) | DEFLATE (RFC 1951), both ways, in pure Nish: a compressor with levels and a decompressor that refuses malformed input with an error code. |
| [`nish/compress/gzip`](compress/gzip.md) | The gzip file format (RFC 1952) around `nish/compress/deflate`: a ten-byte header, the DEFLATE stream, and a trailer of the CRC-32 and the length of the data mod 2^32. |
| [`nish/compress/zlib`](compress/zlib.md) | The zlib format (RFC 1950) around `nish/compress/deflate`: a two-byte header, the DEFLATE stream and the Adler-32 of the data, big-endian. |
| [`nish/crypto/aes`](crypto/aes.md) | AES-128 and AES-256 (FIPS 197), GCM on top of them (NIST SP 800-38D), and QUIC's AES header-protection mask (RFC 9001 §5.4.3). |
| [`nish/crypto/base64url`](crypto/base64url.md) | RFC 4648 §5 base64url, unpadded, as JWS and the relay's grants spell a key or a tag inside a URL or a header. |
| [`nish/crypto/bcrypt-batch`](crypto/bcrypt-batch.md) | A login batcher: it queues bcrypt verifies and hashes as they arrive, sends them as `bcryptVerifyN` / `bcryptHashN` batches, and runs the batches on `std/threads` tasks, one per core. |
| [`nish/crypto/bcrypt`](crypto/bcrypt.md) | Bcrypt password hashing, `$2b$` out and `$2a$`, `$2b$`, `$2y$` in. |
| [`nish/crypto/chacha20poly1305`](crypto/chacha20poly1305.md) | The ChaCha20 stream cipher, the Poly1305 one-time authenticator and the AEAD built from the two, as RFC 8439 defines them, plus the ChaCha20 header-protection mask of RFC 9001 §5.4.4. |
| [`nish/crypto/ct`](crypto/ct.md) | Comparing secrets without telling the clock where they differ. |
| [`nish/crypto/ed25519`](crypto/ed25519.md) | The Ed25519 signature scheme of RFC 8032 (§5.1). |
| [`nish/crypto/hkdf`](crypto/hkdf.md) | HKDF as RFC 5869 defines it, over HMAC-SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-384. |
| [`nish/crypto/hmac`](crypto/hmac.md) | HMAC as RFC 2104 defines it, over SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512. |
| [`nish/crypto/jwt`](crypto/jwt.md) | JSON Web Tokens in the JWS compact serialization: verify one and check its claims, or sign one. |
| [`nish/crypto/p256`](crypto/p256.md) | ECDSA over NIST P-256 (secp256r1), with the deterministic nonces of RFC 6979. |
| [`nish/crypto/p384`](crypto/p384.md) | ECDSA signature verification over NIST P-384 (secp384r1). |
| [`nish/crypto/pki-roots`](crypto/pki-roots.md) | The root certificates a program should trust, read from where OpenSSL and Go look for them: the files `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `SSL_CERT_DIR` name, or else the system's bundle. |
| [`nish/crypto/pki`](crypto/pki.md) | Whether the certificate chain a TLS server sent leads to a root the program trusts and names the host it dialled: RFC 5280 §6 path validation and RFC 6125 §6 hostname matching, at the instant the caller gives. |
| [`nish/crypto/rsa`](crypto/rsa.md) | RSA signature verification: RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 and RSASSA-PSS over SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512, under a public key read from its DER. |
| [`nish/crypto/sha1`](crypto/sha1.md) | SHA-1 as FIPS 180-4 §6.1 defines it, in pure Nish. |
| [`nish/crypto/sha256`](crypto/sha256.md) | SHA-256 as FIPS 180-4 §6.2 defines it, in pure Nish. |
| [`nish/crypto/sha512`](crypto/sha512.md) | SHA-512 and SHA-384, written from FIPS 180-4. |
| [`nish/crypto/x25519`](crypto/x25519.md) | The X25519 Diffie-Hellman function of RFC 7748. |
| [`nish/crypto/x509-random`](crypto/x509-random.md) | The private key and the serial number `nish/crypto/x509`'s `x509MintSelfSigned` needs, drawn from the operating system's CSPRNG, and the mint that draws its own serial. |
| [`nish/crypto/x509`](crypto/x509.md) | DER, PEM and the X.509 certificates a WebTransport or TLS server holds: read a P-256 private key and a certificate chain out of PEM, and mint the short-lived self-signed ECDSA P-256 certificate a browser pins by its SHA-256. |
| [`nish/host/ring`](host/ring.md) | A single-producer, single-consumer ring of `i32` words over module storage, shared by a wasm module and the page that drives it (`docs/wp50-wasm-host.md` §11). |
| [`nish/json-equal`](json-equal.md) | Whether two JSON values are equal by JSON Schema's rule, a canonical text and a hash that agree with it, and the first repeated element of an array, which is what `const`, `enum` and `uniqueItems` ask. |
| [`nish/json-format`](json-format.md) | The string formats of JSON Schema draft 2020-12 (§7.3 of the validation vocabulary), each a predicate, and one dispatcher that answers valid, invalid or unknown for a format named in a schema. |
| [`nish/json-number`](json-number.md) | JSON number text compared and divided exactly, the arithmetic JSON Schema's `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`, `const` and `enum` ask for. |
| [`nish/json-pointer`](json-pointer.md) | RFC 6901 JSON Pointers: parsed into their tokens, escaped, resolved against a `JsonDocument`, and checked, with JSON Schema's relative JSON Pointer beside them. |
| [`nish/json-tokenizer`](json-tokenizer.md) | A validating, streaming tokenizer for RFC 8259 JSON held in a window of a `u8[]`. |
| [`nish/json-typed`](json-typed.md) | Decode a JSON object into a class, and encode a class back, with code the compiler writes from the class's fields. |
| [`nish/json-value`](json-value.md) | Any JSON document as a tree a program can read, build and write back, with every number kept as the text it was written in. |
| [`nish/json`](json.md) | The value of a field, or of several, of one flat JSON object; and `JsonWriter`, which writes any JSON value into a byte buffer. |
| [`nish/map`](map.md) | Two operations on the global `Map` that JavaScript's does not have, written so that a program using them still runs unmodified under Node (docs/wp32-map.md §9.2). |
| [`nish/math`](math.md) | `Math.atan2`, `Math.tan` and `Math.hypot` on `f64`, in Nish rather than libm, so a program answers the same on every target, wasm included, and the optimiser sees the whole function. |
| [`nish/net/buffer-pool`](net/buffer-pool.md) | Fixed-size byte buffers a server's connections borrow and give back, so the memory a server holds follows the connections that are moving bytes, not the slots it was sized for. |
| [`nish/net/dns-config`](net/dns-config.md) | `/etc/resolv.conf` and `/etc/hosts`, read from bytes the caller already has into fixed tables. |
| [`nish/net/dns-message`](net/dns-message.md) | A DNS query for one A or AAAA question written into the caller's buffer, and the reply to it read back into addresses. |
| [`nish/net/dns-resolver`](net/dns-resolver.md) | A DNS stub resolver with no I/O of its own: it says which bytes to send to which server, reads the bytes that came back, and answers each lookup's addresses, while the program's own loop owns the sockets and the clock. |
| [`nish/net/dns`](net/dns.md) | The stub resolver of `nish/net/dns-resolver` driven over `nish:net` sockets on the caller's own readiness loop, and `resolveHost`, which runs a loop of its own for a program that has none. |
| [`nish/net/fetch`](net/fetch.md) | A blocking HTTP/1.1 client for command-line programs: `fetchSync(request, options)` dials, sends, and answers the response's head with a reader for its body, and a `FetchSyncClient` does the same while keeping one connection alive between fetches. |
| [`nish/net/handler`](net/handler.md) | Complete requests and their responses over the HTTP/1.1 carrier, so that a server answers requests instead of driving `Http1Server`'s events by hand. |
| [`nish/net/hpack`](net/hpack.md) | HPACK, the header compression of HTTP/2, as RFC 7541 defines it: the §5.1 integer with an N-bit prefix, the §5.2 string literal with Appendix B's Huffman code, the Appendix A static table, the §2.3.2 dynamic table with its §4 size accounting and eviction, and the four §6 representations. |
| [`nish/net/http-compress`](net/http-compress.md) | Content coding for HTTP responses (RFC 9110 §8.4 and §12.5.3): reading a request's `Accept-Encoding` and compressing a body with `Content-Encoding: gzip`, for any of the three servers. |
| [`nish/net/http-fields`](net/http-fields.md) | The header model HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 share: what a field name and a field value may hold, the pseudo-header fields and the order and count they come in, the connection-specific fields neither version carries, and the shapes of a request, a response and a trailer section. |
| [`nish/net/http1-client-codec`](net/http1-client-codec.md) | The client side of HTTP/1.1, sans-IO: a request writer and an incremental response parser, bytes in, events and bytes out, and no socket anywhere. |
| [`nish/net/http1-codec`](net/http1-codec.md) | An incremental HTTP/1.1 request parser and a response writer, sans-IO: bytes in, events and bytes out, and no socket anywhere. |
| [`nish/net/http1-server`](net/http1-server.md) | The server side of HTTP/1.1 (RFC 9112): a sans-IO connection that drives `nish/net/http1-codec`'s parser, and two pools of them for a program that owns its readiness loop, one on `nish:net`'s plain TCP and one on `nish/net/tls-tcp` with ALPN `http/1.1`. |
| [`nish/net/http2-frame`](net/http2-frame.md) | The frames of HTTP/2 (RFC 9113 §4 and §6): the nine-byte header, every one of the ten frame types read and written, and the size, flag, padding and stream-identifier rules each one carries. |
| [`nish/net/http2-tls`](net/http2-tls.md) | HTTP/2 over TLS 1.3 on TCP: a pool of `Http2Connection`s, one beside each slot of a `TlsTcpServer`, for a program that owns its readiness loop. |
| [`nish/net/http2`](net/http2.md) | The server side of an HTTP/2 connection (RFC 9113): the connection preface, SETTINGS and their acknowledgement, the stream state machine of §5.1, flow control on the connection and on every stream with WINDOW_UPDATE, PING, RST_STREAM, GOAWAY with the last stream identifier, header blocks across CONTINUATION frames decoded by `nish/net/hpack`, and extended CONNECT (RFC 8441). |
| [`nish/net/http3-frame`](net/http3-frame.md) | The frames and stream types of HTTP/3 (RFC 9114 §6.2, §7): frame headers, SETTINGS, the one-identifier frames (GOAWAY, MAX_PUSH_ID, CANCEL_PUSH), and which types are HTTP/2's reserved ones or unknown. |
| [`nish/net/http3-server`](net/http3-server.md) | HTTP/3 over QUIC on one UDP socket: a pool of slots, each a reusable `QuicConnection` with an `Http3Connection` beside it, a `QuicListener` in front for the datagrams no slot owns, for a program that owns its readiness loop. |
| [`nish/net/http3`](net/http3.md) | The server side of an HTTP/3 connection (RFC 9114) on the streams of a `QuicConnection` (`nish/net/quic`): the control stream and SETTINGS both ways, the QPACK encoder and decoder streams (opened, at dynamic table capacity 0), requests and responses on bidirectional streams with their bodies streamed both ways, GOAWAY, and RFC 9114's error codes. |
| [`nish/net/outbound`](net/outbound.md) | The policy for a program that fetches URLs it did not choose: a webhook sender, a link previewer, an importer that takes a URL from a form. |
| [`nish/net/postgres-carrier`](net/postgres-carrier.md) | `PgCarrier`, a `PgPool`'s queries on an `HttpHandler`'s loop, so a route handler queries PostgreSQL without blocking its worker. |
| [`nish/net/postgres`](net/postgres.md) | The client side of PostgreSQL's frontend/backend protocol, version 3.0: a sans-IO connection that writes the frontend's messages into an output buffer and reads the backend's from an input buffer, for a program that owns its socket (`nish:net`) and its loop. |
| [`nish/net/prefork`](net/prefork.md) | Run a server on every core: a supervisor process that starts one worker process per core, restarts one that dies, and stops them all on SIGTERM or SIGINT (`docs/wp42-multicore-server.md` §2.3). |
| [`nish/net/qpack`](net/qpack.md) | QPACK, the field compression of HTTP/3, as RFC 9204 defines it with a dynamic table of capacity 0: the Appendix A static table, the §4.1.1 prefixed integer up to 62 bits, the §4.1.2 string literal with an N-bit prefix, the §4.5 field-line representations under a Required Insert Count of 0, and what the encoder and decoder streams of §4.2 may carry when neither side ever inserts. |
| [`nish/net/quic-conn-ack`](net/quic-conn-ack.md) | The packet numbers one QUIC packet number space has received, kept as ranges, which is what duplicate detection reads (RFC 9000 §12.3) and what an ACK frame is written from (§13.2, §19.3). |
| [`nish/net/quic-conn-cid`](net/quic-conn-cid.md) | A QUIC connection's connection-ID table (RFC 9000 §5.1): the IDs this endpoint issued, which a datagram is routed by, and the ones the peer issued, which this endpoint sends to. |
| [`nish/net/quic-conn-params`](net/quic-conn-params.md) | QUIC's transport parameters (RFC 9000 §18), the bytes each endpoint carries in TLS's `quic_transport_parameters` extension (RFC 9001 §8.2), encoded and parsed. |
| [`nish/net/quic-datagram`](net/quic-datagram.md) | A fixed ring of QUIC DATAGRAM payloads (RFC 9221), one each way per connection: what the application queued to send, waiting for room in a packet and in the congestion window, and what the peer sent, waiting for the application to read it. |
| [`nish/net/quic-frame`](net/quic-frame.md) | The frames of QUIC version 1 (RFC 9000 §19) and RFC 9221's DATAGRAM, read from a decrypted packet payload and written into one, and the transport error codes a connection closes with (§20.1). |
| [`nish/net/quic-listener`](net/quic-listener.md) | What a QUIC version 1 server answers to a datagram no connection owns: Version Negotiation for a version it does not speak (RFC 9000 §6, §17.2.1), a Retry that asks a client to prove its address before any connection state exists (§8.1.2, §17.2.5), and a stateless reset for a packet sent to a connection the server no longer has (§10.3). |
| [`nish/net/quic-packet`](net/quic-packet.md) | QUIC version 1's packets, as RFC 9000 §16-§17 frames them and RFC 9001 §5 protects them: the variable-length integer, the long and short headers, packet-number encoding and recovery, the Initial secrets, AEAD packet protection, header protection and the Retry integrity tag. |
| [`nish/net/quic-recovery`](net/quic-recovery.md) | QUIC loss detection and congestion control (RFC 9002): the packets each packet number space has in flight, the round-trip estimate, loss by packet and by time threshold, the probe timeout with its backoff, NewReno, and a pacer. |
| [`nish/net/quic-stream`](net/quic-stream.md) | The streams of one QUIC version 1 connection (RFC 9000 §2-§4): stream IDs and their four types, the sending and receiving state machines, reassembly, flow control per stream and for the connection, and the stream limits. |
| [`nish/net/quic`](net/quic.md) | The server side of a QUIC version 1 connection (RFC 9000, RFC 9001, RFC 9221): the TLS 1.3 handshake carried in CRYPTO frames at three encryption levels, transport parameters both ways, acknowledgements per packet number space, the connection-ID table, streams both ways (`nish/net/quic-stream`) and DATAGRAM frames once the handshake is done. |
| [`nish/net/router`](net/router.md) | A method and path router for HTTP servers, independent of the carrier: the same table answers an HTTP/1 request line and an HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 `:path`. |
| [`nish/net/tls-tcp`](net/tls-tcp.md) | TLS 1.3 over TCP (WP34 T2): a pool of server connections on `nish:net`, each a `TlsRecordServer` driving a `TlsServer`, for a program that owns its readiness loop; and `TlsTcpClient`, one client connection that authenticates the server (`nish/net/tls/verify`) and is driven by the same kind of loop or, through `tlsConnect`, `readWait` and `writeAll`, by none (its own comment, below, says how). |
| [`nish/net/tls`](net/tls.md) | The server side of a TLS 1.3 handshake (RFC 8446), from the client's first ClientHello to its Finished, carrier-agnostic and sans-IO. |
| [`nish/net/tls/client`](net/tls/client.md) | The client side of a TLS 1.3 handshake (RFC 8446), from its ClientHello to its Finished, carrier-agnostic and sans-IO: the mirror of `nish/net/tls`'s `TlsServer`. |
| [`nish/net/tls/codec`](net/tls/codec.md) | The TLS 1.3 handshake messages a server and a client read and write (RFC 8446 §4), as bytes. |
| [`nish/net/tls/record-client`](net/tls/record-client.md) | A TLS 1.3 client over a byte stream: the record layer of `nish/net/tls/record` wrapped around `nish/net/tls/client`'s `TlsClient`, sans-IO. |
| [`nish/net/tls/record-server`](net/tls/record-server.md) | A TLS 1.3 server over a byte stream: the record layer of `nish/net/tls/record` wrapped around `nish/net/tls`'s `TlsServer`, sans-IO. |
| [`nish/net/tls/record`](net/tls/record.md) | The TLS 1.3 record layer (RFC 8446 §5): the framing of a byte stream into records, the protection of one direction of it under a traffic secret, and the next secret a KeyUpdate moves to. |
| [`nish/net/tls/schedule`](net/tls/schedule.md) | The TLS 1.3 key schedule and transcript hash (RFC 8446 §4.4.1, §7.1, §7.3) for the three cipher suites `nish/net/tls` negotiates. |
| [`nish/net/tls/ticket`](net/tls/ticket.md) | TLS 1.3 session tickets a server seals for itself (RFC 8446 §4.6.1), and the strike register that makes each one single-use (§8.1). |
| [`nish/net/tls/verify`](net/tls/verify.md) | The TLS client's one authentication seam: whether the server a `TlsRecordClient` reached is the one its `serverName` says, decided at `TLS_RECORD_AUTH` and handed to the connection as its verdict. |
| [`nish/net/upstream`](net/upstream.md) | Outbound HTTP/1.1 calls from a route handler that never block its worker: a pool of keep-alive connections to one origin, registered on the `HttpHandler`'s own poll loop and read through the `nish/net/http1-client-codec` codec. |
| [`nish/net/url`](net/url.md) | The request target's path and query, split and percent-decoded in place, and its query string read as key/value pairs; and whole URLs, parsed into their parts and references resolved against them. |
| [`nish/net/websocket`](net/websocket.md) | RFC 6455 WebSocket framing and both sides of the opening handshake, sans-IO: bytes in, events and bytes out. |
| [`nish/net/webtransport`](net/webtransport.md) | WebTransport over HTTP/3, server side, as draft-ietf-webtrans-http3-02 has it and as Chrome and the `wtransport` 0.7 crate negotiate it: sessions made by an extended CONNECT (RFC 9220) with `:protocol` `webtransport`, HTTP datagrams (RFC 9297) carrying the session's quarter stream ID, the session's unidirectional and bidirectional streams, and CLOSE_WEBTRANSPORT_SESSION and DRAIN_WEBTRANSPORT_SESSION on the CONNECT stream's capsules. |
| [`nish/pair`](pair.md) | Two values answered by one call. |
| [`nish/random`](random.md) | A seeded generator of pseudo-random numbers whose every answer is the same natively and under Node. |
| [`nish/regex`](regex.md) | Regular expressions whose search time is linear in the input, whatever the pattern. |
| [`nish/sort`](sort.md) | `xs.sort(cmp)` on an array, in Nish: a stable merge sort, compiled once per comparator. |
| [`nish/sqlite`](sqlite.md) | `nish/sqlite` (the file `std/sqlite.ts`) — SQLite, the database in a file, from a Nish program. |
| [`nish/sync/ring`](sync/ring.md) | Bounded lock-free queues of byte records in a shared region, for handing work between processes on different cores. |
| [`nish/sync/shm`](sync/shm.md) | Memory that several processes map at once, and the atomics that order what they write to it. |
| [`nish/term-io`](term-io.md) | Opening a terminal, drawing frames, reading events and leaving it as it was: the one entry point that uses the other term modules and does the I/O. |
| [`nish/term-pixels`](term-pixels.md) | A framebuffer of pixels, and the encoders that draw it to a terminal with the best backend the terminal has: kitty graphics, Sixel, half-block cells or ASCII. |
| [`nish/term-probe`](term-probe.md) | What the terminal a program runs in can do (its colours, keyboard protocol, graphics and size), asked of it once at start and read from its answer. |
| [`nish/term-rate`](term-rate.md) | How fast the link to the terminal is, measured from frames sent and acknowledged, and the frame rate and drawing detail a program keeps to under it. |
| [`nish/term`](term.md) | A terminal drawn as a grid of coloured cells, and the keys a terminal sends turned into events. |
| [`nish/testing`](testing.md) | A test runner for Nish programs, written in Nish. |
| [`nish/text`](text.md) | The string operations a program has to write itself. |
| [`nish/threads`](threads.md) | Data parallelism, a scope for heterogeneous tasks, and a lock that owns its data (docs/wp29-thread-surface.md §4.1, §4.2 and §4.3). |
| [`nish/yaml-json`](yaml-json.md) | One YAML document loaded into a `JsonDocument`, with every value's and key's source range, so that one validator and one `YamlLineIndex` serve a JSON text and a YAML text alike: |
| [`nish/yaml-lines`](yaml-lines.md) | Byte offsets turned into the `line:column` a person reads. |
| [`nish/yaml-write`](yaml-write.md) | A JSON value written as YAML text that `parseYaml` reads back as the same tree. |
| [`nish/yaml`](yaml.md) | A YAML 1.2 parser that keeps where everything came from. |
